audora.purpose: The brand spine. Runs through every primary action, active state, focus ring, and console highlight. The only accent hue.

surface.purpose: The near-black, faintly blue solid backgrounds the glass floats over. Never flat — an ambient violet/fuchsia wash glows behind them.

console.purpose: Skeuomorphic material used ONLY on the download receiver: brushed-metal shell, recessed phosphor-green LCD, amber in-flight glow. Its power is its singularity — never spread elsewhere.

emerald.purpose: Semantic success only — completed steps, terminal 'done' lines, success headlines.

rose.purpose: Semantic failure and interruption — error icons/lines, failure panels, the destructive Stop-download transport.

amber.purpose: Semantic attention — the 'Extracting' phase and mid-process readouts.

wordmarkGradient.purpose: APPROVED BRAND GRADIENT 1 of 2. linear-gradient(90deg, #cabeb0 0%, #e09e52 100%), clipped to text, paired only with Caveat 700, used only on the Audora wordmark. Intentionally outside the violet spine: the single warm object in a cool app, which is what lets a small lockup hold its own against the ambient violet wash. Text-only — never a fill.

logoSoundwave.purpose: APPROVED BRAND GRADIENT 2 of 2. #4A8FD6 → #A78BC9, matching the soundwave bars in the Audora logo. Used only as a solid fill: the setup progress-bar fill (to-r) and the sign-in avatar mark (to-br). Replaced an earlier violet→fuchsia fill that was never verified against the logo artwork. Fill-only — never text.

sans.purpose: All interface text: labels, headings, body, buttons. Weight tops out at semibold (the wordmark is the only bold exception).

mono.purpose: Measurement and machine output only: the terminal, the receiver LCD, byte counts, timers, percentages, the source-link input. Signals 'this is a real value.'

eyebrow.purpose: Small all-caps labels above inputs and readouts: text-[10px]/[11px] uppercase, tracking 0.16em–0.2em. A signature that makes tiny labels feel engineered.

wordmark.purpose: The wordmark face and nothing else — the one handwritten gesture in an app of machined surfaces; its scarcity is the point. Self-hosted latin-subset woff2 (not a CDN link) because the app runs offline over file://. Sized up (~1.6–2rem) with leading-[1.15] and no negative tracking, since Caveat reads optically smaller than Inter and tight tracking damages a connected script.

shadows.name: glass
shadows.purpose: Floating glass panels — nav, cards, player bar.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Surfaces that rise above their neighbors.

shadows.name: console
shadows.purpose: The download receiver — heaviest object in the app; sits on the stage like a real device.

shadows.name: knob
shadows.purpose: Tactile shadow under every primary button and transport control, so they read as physical.

shadows.name: readout-inset
shadows.purpose: Recessed depth for the LCD readout and input wells — carved into the panel, not floating.

shadows.name: glass-highlight
shadows.purpose: Top-edge light-catch overlay on every glass pane (::before). Content inside must be relative z-10 to sit above it.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The shared easing — a confident settle used on nearly every transition.

motion.name: slide-in-left
motion.purpose: The download receiver arriving on the Download page.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce collapses all animation/transition to ~0.01ms
motion.purpose: Every motion decision must survive this toggle.

backdropFilter.name: glass
backdropFilter.purpose: The frost. The saturate boost lets the ambient wash bleed through as color rather than gray.

atmosphere.name: ambient-wash
atmosphere.value: radial-gradient(60rem 40rem at 12% -10%, rgba(124,92,191,0.20), transparent 70%), radial-gradient(48rem 32rem at 96% 8%, rgba(192,84,178,0.14), transparent 68%), radial-gradient(52rem 44rem at 50% 108%, rgba(67,44,122,0.22), transparent 72%)
atmosphere.purpose: Fixed violet/fuchsia glow behind everything. Without something to refract, frosted glass reads as flat gray.

narrative.overview: Audora is a listening-room console, not a web dashboard. Every surface is a pane of frosted glass floating over a deep violet wash — you sense depth and light passing through, never a flat gray card. The one exception is deliberate and load-bearing: the Download page is a physical receiver, a brushed-metal panel with a recessed LCD, because tuning in a download and watching it arrive should feel like operating a real device. This is an Operate system: the visitor's success is completing a task — signing in, tuning in a download, playing a track, recovering from a failed setup step. Scanability, consistency, and honest state reporting outrank expression. The brand does not shout; it lives in precise details: the violet spine that runs through every primary action, the top-edge highlight on every glass pane, the monospaced readouts that treat numbers as measurement. The one place the brand speaks in its own voice is the wordmark — Caveat 700 in a warm sand-to-amber gradient, the single handwritten and single warm object in an app otherwise built from cool machined surfaces. It earns that licence by being scarce: one word, three places, nowhere else.
keyCharacteristics: Frosted glass over an ambient violet/fuchsia wash — depth via translucency, shadow, and top-edge light at once
A single violet brand spine (the audora ramp) through every primary action, active state, and focus ring
One deliberate skeuomorphic moment: the download receiver with its recessed phosphor-green LCD
Monospace for anything that is real measurement or machine output; Inter for everything else
A scarce script wordmark: Caveat 700 in a warm sand→amber gradient, the one handwritten and one warm object in a cool machined app
A first-class, always-visible terminal as a trust surface
Fixed Windows desktop canvas (1400x900, min 1200x800) — no responsive reflow

rules.name: The One Spine Rule
rules.body: Violet (the audora ramp) is the only brand accent. Run it through every primary action, active state, and focus ring; never introduce a second competing accent hue.

rules.name: The Two Gradients Rule
rules.body: Exactly two multi-color gradients are approved, and they are not interchangeable. (1) The WORDMARK gradient: linear-gradient(90deg, #cabeb0 0%, #e09e52 100%), clipped to text, paired only with Caveat 700, used only on the Audora wordmark via the .wordmark class. It sits deliberately outside the violet spine — the one warm object in a cool app — and must not be harmonized back toward violet. (2) The PROGRESS/AVATAR gradient: #4A8FD6 → #A78BC9 (blue→lavender, matching the logo's soundwave bars), used only as a solid fill on the setup progress bar and the sign-in avatar mark. Never swap them: sand→amber is text-only, blue→lavender is fill-only. Never add a third.

rules.name: The Scarce Script Rule
rules.body: Caveat 700 is loaded for one word. It appears only on the Audora wordmark lockup (top nav, About, and the unmounted Sidebar) — never on headings, labels, body copy, numbers, or prose that merely contains the name. It is self-hosted (frontend/src/assets/fonts/caveat-700.woff2) rather than loaded from a CDN, because this is an offline-capable Electron app over file:// and a network fallback would silently break the lockup.

rules.name: The Real Value Rule
rules.body: Use font-mono + tabular-nums for anything that is a real, updating value; never fabricate progress, frequencies, or state — every readout reflects actual data.

rules.name: The Glass Highlight Rule
rules.body: Every .glass pane carries a ::before top-edge highlight that sits above the panel background, so interactive content inside must be wrapped relative z-10 or the highlight will cover it.

rules.name: The Singular Skeuomorph Rule
rules.body: The receiver's brushed metal and phosphor-green LCD live only on the Download page. Its impact is its singularity — never spread the material to other surfaces.

rules.name: The Single Recovery Path Rule
rules.body: When a step fails, present exactly one primary recovery button (Retry). Never two competing recovery actions, never a dead-end error, and never an instruction to open a terminal or run a command.

dos: Do compose the .glass utility for every translucent surface; keep the recipe in one place.
Do wrap content inside .glass in relative z-10 so the top-edge highlight stays behind it.
Do keep the ambient wash behind everything — it is what makes the glass read as glass.
Do run the violet spine (audora.500/400) through every primary action, active state, and focus ring.
Do use font-mono + tabular-nums for anything that is a real, updating value.
Do report state with the fixed semantic colors: emerald = done, rose = failure, amber = in-flight.
Do keep the terminal a first-class, styled instrument on the surfaces that have one.
Do enforce the single-recovery-path rule on every failure state.
Do design for exactly 1400x900 (min 1200x800) — one confident desktop canvas.
Do render the wordmark only through the .wordmark class, so the face and gradient stay identical everywhere.
Do self-host brand fonts — a CDN link would silently drop the lockup to a fallback face whenever the user is offline.
donts: Don't paint flat bg-gray-900 cards or raw gray-*/violet-* surfaces — that is the pre-redesign look and the anti-reference.
Don't introduce a second brand accent hue; violet is the only spine.
Don't recolor, re-letter, or re-face the wordmark: it is Caveat 700 with the #cabeb0 → #e09e52 gradient, always via the .wordmark class.
Don't set Caveat on anything that isn't the wordmark, and don't apply .wordmark to prose that merely contains the word 'Audora'.
Don't swap the two brand gradients — sand→amber is text-only (wordmark), blue→lavender is fill-only (progress bar, avatar) — and don't add a third.
Don't spread the skeuomorphic material (brushed metal, phosphor green) beyond the download receiver.
Don't put a mid-gray on a saturated color fill; use white or a near-white tint.
Don't show two competing recovery buttons, a dead-end error, or any 'open a terminal / run this command' instruction.
Don't render anything that could contain an Apple ID or password unredacted.
Don't add mobile breakpoints, responsive reflow, or copy that implies cross-platform or web deployment — this is a Windows desktop app.
Don't drop the upstream credit to zhaarey/apple-music-downloader and WorldObservationLog/wrapper.
